The loop-carried RAW on array elements of `v` is the blocker. Line 6 reads `v[kv[i]]` (from earlier iterations' line 7 writes to `v[jv[j]]`), and line 7 writes `v[jv[i]]`. This cross-iteration dependency on `v` prevents parallelization.

**The fix:**
The evidence indicates "the update travels along the array as the sweep runs" — values written to `v` in line 7 are read again by line 6 in later iterations. Per the guidance, I split into ordered sub-passes over the two statements.

**Restructuring approach:**
Split the single loop into two sequential loops:
1. **First loop:** all line 6 operations (read initial `v`, update `u`)
2. **Second loop:** all line 7 operations (read updated `u`, update `v`)

This separation removes the cross-iteration dependence on `v` within each loop. Each loop can then be independently analyzed by DiscoPoP. The first loop reads `v` without modifying it (parallelizable if no index aliasing), and the second loop reads the just-computed `u` values and updates `v` without internal carries (also potentially parallelizable).
